A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScoreMix and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original face-recognition experiments, class-selection and alignment analyses, generated examples, and empirical validation of geometric order preservation.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds cross-selector experiments, sampling and reproduction controls, ImageNet-1K evaluation, and a preliminary CUB-200 experiment.

M1.justification: The convex score-mixing algorithm and face-recognition method remain intact. Section 5 and Appendix R add an ImageNet adaptation using soft-label cross-entropy over existing classes. The new explanation that face mixtures receive separate synthetic identity labels clarifies the existing procedure without establishing that it changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual ImageNet-1K object-classification and CUB-200 fine-grained bird-recognition experiments, substantially extending the previously face-focused evaluation. The original face-training data and eight face-recognition benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged. Appendix L adds a targeted comparison against three non-mixing controls: reproductions assigned to original classes, reproductions assigned to new classes, and dummy classifier centers without training samples.

E3.justification: New protocols vary selector–target combinations, guidance scales of 1.3 and 2.7, sampler steps of 32 and 50, and reproduction-label assignments and classifier sizes. ImageNet introduces 128×128 inputs, two classifier backbones, and 25-epoch soft-label training. The retained face-recognition hyperparameter table is unchanged; the added fixed-compute explanation does not establish a rerun of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices H–L add direct cross-selector transfer tests, guidance and denoising-step sensitivity studies, a computational-cost analysis, source-proximity and compactness diagnostics, and controls separating mixing from non-mixed reproductions. These investigate substantive questions beyond the retained class-selection, alignment, and multi-class-mixing analyses.

E5.justification: v2 already reports fixed seeds and across-class variability for diagnostic metrics. v3 extends uncertainty reporting to training outcomes: Table 11 gives means and standard deviations over repeated runs, and Appendix R specifies two seeds for ImageNet. The face-control repeat count is unspecified, and the original main performance tables retain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and v2 Table 2, now v3 Table 3, retain their numerical results. v3 adds extensive transfer, sensitivity, control, timing, and hardness results. Its new ImageNet comparisons report 43.53% versus 44.53% for ResNet50 and 45.07% versus 46.00% for FastViT-S12. New CUB results are 25.80% for baseline, 24.46% for AugGen, and 23.04% for ScoreMix. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The CKA theorem, Gaussian misalignment assumptions, corollaries, and proofs are retained with equivalent mathematics and renumbered equations. Appendix K makes a limited mathematical addition by defining the source-distance diagnostic in Equation 28 for the new hardness analysis.

C1.justification: The central score-mixing, distant-class-selection, and up-to-seven-percentage-point face-recognition claims remain. The abstract narrows the condition-space statement from negligible downstream effect to weak correlation between condition distances and gains. The conclusion adds preliminary applicability beyond faces while acknowledging the unsuccessful fine-grained setting.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting sample hardness to source-boundary proximity and compactness, practical CKA-based transfer guidance, and a generator-quality limitation motivated by CUB. It reframes sampling overhead relative to AugGen's search cost. It also corrects the description of the retained 2.52 difference from a pairwise distance to a performance difference.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation through explicit synthetic-class labeling, baseline provenance, matched-budget explanations, the 37M-image generator-training budget, sampling hardware and timing breakdowns, and ImageNet architecture and training details. Appendix R identifies the existing ImageNet-trained generator checkpoint. Code and synthetic-data release remain promises rather than newly established availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and positioning relative to AugGen and compositional diffusion remain unchanged. Revisions to the Huh et al. and AugGen bibliography entries update their titles or metadata while retaining their citation roles; they do not establish a substantive change in research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract and selected explanatory passages while retaining most existing prose and its narrative sequence. It renames the experimental section, adds a separate ImageNet section, demotes the alignment subsection, relocates empirical theorem validation and disclosure statements, and updates author and publication text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a predominantly single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with substantially resized and repositioned figures and tables. Original figure graphics are retained. New tables display transfer, sensitivity, cost, hardness, reproduction controls, and non-face results; the transfer summary is also repeated in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central mechanism: Appendix L addresses whether gains require mixing rather than merely more generated images, and Appendix H directly tests cross-model selection. Added uncertainty reporting, labeling details, and cost breakdowns reduce important interpretability and reproducibility gaps in v2. Positive ImageNet and negative CUB results better delineate applicability. The non-face evidence remains preliminary, with only two ImageNet seeds and an existing generator checkpoint, but these limitations are explicitly acknowledged.
